paper_title: XAttention: Block Sparse Attention with Antidiagonal Scoring
abstract: Long-Context Transformer Models (LCTMs) are vital for real-world applications but suffer high computational costs due to attention's quadratic complexity. Block-sparse attention mitigates this by focusing computation on critical regions, yet existing methods struggle with balancing accuracy and efficiency due to costly block importance measurements. In this paper, we introduce XAttention, a plug-and-play framework that dramatically accelerates long-context inference in Transformers models using sparse attention. XAttention's key innovation is the insight that the sum of antidiagonal values (i.e., from the lower-left to upper-right) in the attention matrix provides a powerful proxy for block importance. This allows for precise identification and pruning of non-essential blocks, resulting in high sparsity and dramatically accelerated inference. Across comprehensive evaluations on demanding long-context benchmarks—including RULER and LongBench for language, VideoMME for video understanding, and VBench for video generation—XAttention achieves accuracy comparable to full attention while delivering substantial computational gains. We demonstrate up to 13.5× acceleration in attention computation. These results underscore XAttention's ability to unlock the practical potential of block sparse attention, paving the way for scalable and efficient deployment of LCTMs in real-world applications.

innovative_points.explanation: Uses the sum of antidiagonal values in attention blocks as a computationally efficient proxy for block importance. This approach intersects both vertical and slash patterns within blocks, ensuring comprehensive pattern detection while maintaining O(L²/S) complexity for pattern selection.
innovative_points.runtime_change: [L, d, L/S] where S is the stride parameter (typically 8 or 16)

innovative_points.innovation: Dynamic Threshold Prediction via Dynamic Programming
innovative_points.explanation: Employs a dynamic programming approach to determine optimal sparsity thresholds for individual attention heads. Uses recurrence relation D[h][m] = max(D[h-1][m], P(h,m)) with gradual threshold reduction (10% steps) across M=1000 adjustments.
innovative_points.runtime_change: [H, 1, M] where H=number of heads, M=1000 adjustments

innovative_points.explanation: Provides plug-and-play capability without requiring model retraining. Achieves sparse attention through runtime pattern selection based on antidiagonal scoring, eliminating the need for pretraining or fine-tuning.
innovative_points.runtime_change: No communication overhead - [L, d, L·ρ] where ρ is the sparsity ratio (6.2-55.4%)

innovative_points.explanation: Introduces a 5-step full attention warmup phase for video generation to maintain layout consistency, followed by sparse attention for remaining denoising steps. Addresses the challenge of applying sparse attention to diffusion models.
innovative_points.runtime_change: 5×[L, d, L] + (T-5)×[L, d, L·ρ] where T=total denoising steps

innovative_points.explanation: Comprehensive evaluation across three distinct domains (natural language, video understanding, video generation) using consistent methodology, demonstrating universal applicability of the antidiagonal scoring approach.
innovative_points.runtime_change: Domain-agnostic [L, d, L·ρ] computation across Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2-VL-7B, and HunyuanVideo

proposed_improvements.description: Combine antidiagonal with diagonal, vertical, and horizontal patterns using learned weights for more robust importance prediction
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [L, d, L·P/S] where P=4 patterns (vs [L, d, L/S] original)

proposed_improvements.description: Dynamically adjust block sizes based on attention head characteristics and sequence length using hierarchical blocks
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [L/B_h, d, B_h²] with adaptive B_h per head (vs fixed [L/B, d, B²])

proposed_improvements.description: Use neural network to predict optimal stride based on input characteristics and domain type
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [L, d, L/S_optimal] where S_optimal is learned (vs discrete S ∈ {4,8,16,64})

proposed_improvements.description: Replace dynamic programming with gradient-based optimization and head grouping for faster threshold selection
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: [H/G, 1, K] gradient steps (vs [H, 1, M=1000] DP iterations)

proposed_improvements.description: Replace fixed warmup with progressive sparsity increase during denoising using content-aware schedules
proposed_improvements.expected_benefit: Eliminates warmup overhead while maintaining quality

proposed_improvements.description: Learn domain-invariant pattern representations with shared pattern bank and lightweight domain-specific adaptation
proposed_improvements.runtime_change: Shared [L, d, L/S] pattern selection + domain-specific adaptation layers
proposed_improvements.expected_benefit: 30% reduction in total parameters with maintained multi-domain performance

runtime_comparison.original_xattention: [L, d, L·ρ] + [L, d, L/S] - achieves 13.5× speedup at 256K tokens
runtime_comparison.improved_xattention: [L, d, L·ρ'] + [L, d, L/S'] - projected 18-22× speedup with ρ' < ρ, S' < S
